models.note: The offline stub bills nothing: no provider is called. Its token figures are the stub's own declared per-call figures (150 input tokens per call; 40 output tokens for a tool call, 60 for a text reply), not measured provider metering, so every figure priced from them is an estimate. The rates are a shadow price — this table's openai:gpt-5.1 list rate — so an offline run can be compared with a real one. An offline case's cost is always labelled estimated and is never a provider figure.

OpenAI published list rate for gpt-5.1, checked 2026-10-17. Prompt-caching discounts are not modelled: cached input is priced at the full input rate, so a cached run's ledger figure reads high against its invoice, never low.
Anthropic published list rate for claude-sonnet-4-5, checked 2026-10-17. Prompt-caching and batch discounts are not modelled, as with the OpenAI entry.

A self-hosted local model: no per-token provider charge exists to record. The hardware and power it ran on are real costs, but they are not per-token figures and this table does not invent any — the ledger prices this model at zero and says why.

note: The governed price table for cost accounting. Rates are USD per million tokens, held as data and versioned like the harness profiles: a price change is a new version of this file, never an edit to a recorded ledger — every cost line recorded on a case carries the table version and the rates it was priced with, so raising the version here re-prices nothing that already ran. Provider rates below are the providers' published list rates as checked when this version was written; they are the desk's costing basis, not a provider invoice — what a provider actually billed is a finance record, not this ledger. A model with no entry here is recorded as unpriced, never silently priced at an invented rate.
